articles.title: Alligator Hide
articles.summary: Dense leathery plates with deep dark fissures; per-plate sparkle, micro-pitted surface A fine, even leathery or brick grain; at distance it is a quiet pebbled satin texture that only shows in the highlight.
articles.what: Fine 8-14 px rectangular leathery plates packed dense, deep dark M=low fissure cracks between plates, per-plate independent M/R/CC, sub-plate 2-3 px micro-pitting, M=Meta Up close: Neat brick-bond rows of small rounded rectangular plates about 14 px wide, each a slightly raised pad, separated by thin dark seams. Rows are straight and offset like brickwork; no big shapes, plates are evenly lit. From a distance: A fine, even leathery or brick grain; at distance it is a quiet pebbled satin texture that only shows in the highlight. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: metal, roughness, clearcoat. Group: Predator Skins (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Predator Skins", or search for "Alligator Hide".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof and doors: rows read cleanly on flat panels
Sides as a background under graphics
Numbers stay fully legible; the grid is too fine to disturb them.
Gentle: plates lift out of the satin as faint bright tiles inside the highlight
Pairs well with: matte, metallic, satin, gloss.
pitfalls: Not a brick wall paint pattern: no colour, no mortar tint, only shine tiles
Not the Alligator Coat spec: this has soft rounded pads in brick rows, not slanted blocks with lips
Avoid: very dense, avoid small panels, sparkle fights bright colours.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.
